effects: The host session becomes unlocked and, on a fresh directory, the submitted passphrase verifier is stored.
Host-only controls on the setup and console surfaces become available until the session is locked or the process restarts.

failures.condition: The submitted passphrase does not match the stored verifier.
failures.recovery: Re-enter the host passphrase; repeated failures still leave member voting and tally reads available.
failures.response: The unlock is rejected as host_auth_failed, the session stays locked, and the attempt counter increments.

failures.condition: A passphrase is being set on a fresh directory but is blank or shorter than four characters.
failures.recovery: Choose a nonblank passphrase of at least four characters and submit again.
failures.response: The unlock is rejected as passphrase_invalid and no verifier is stored.

actions.name: Unlock host mode
preconditions: The caller is the host at the shared device and knows the host passphrase, or is on a fresh directory where no passphrase has been set yet.
No other unlock attempt is mid-write on this device.

effects: The host session becomes locked and host-only controls disappear from every surface.
Poll status, ballots, events, and counts are unchanged, and member voting and tally reads continue without a session.

failures.condition: The host session is already locked or unset.
failures.recovery: Proceed with member voting; unlock host mode again when a host transition is needed.
failures.response: The lock is reported as already_locked and nothing changes.

actions.name: Lock host mode
preconditions: The host session is unlocked.
No host transition is mid-write.

effects: A poll row is stored with status open and created_at set.
One option row per accepted label is stored with a stable poll-scoped id and display position.
A created event is appended and the tally starts provisional with every option at zero.
The new poll becomes the active voting target in the directory store.

failures.condition: Fewer than 2 or more than 8 options are submitted.
failures.recovery: Adjust the list to at least 2 and at most 8 distinct labels and resubmit.
failures.response: Creation is rejected as option_count_invalid and nothing is stored.

failures.condition: An option label is blank or duplicates another label after trimming and case folding.
failures.recovery: Rename or remove the duplicate or blank entry, then resubmit.
failures.response: Creation is rejected as option_label_invalid, naming the offending label, and no poll and no partial option set are stored.

failures.condition: The question text is blank.
failures.recovery: Enter the dinner question and resubmit.
failures.response: Creation is rejected as question_required and nothing is stored.

failures.condition: The host session is locked.
failures.recovery: Unlock host mode with the passphrase, then submit the question and options again.
failures.response: Creation is rejected as host_mode_required and nothing is stored.

actions.name: Create dinner poll
preconditions: The host session is unlocked on this device.
A nonblank question and between 2 and 8 distinct place labels are supplied.
No other creation is mid-write on this device.

effects: If no ballot exists for this poll and code, a ballot row is stored with cast_at and revision 1.
If a ballot already exists for this poll and code, its option is replaced in place, revision increments, and cast_at is retained.
The tally is recomputed and returned; total ballots increases only when a first ballot is created.

failures.condition: The poll is closed.
failures.recovery: Ask the host to reopen the poll, then submit again with the same code.
failures.response: The write is rejected with response poll_closed and no ballot row is created or changed.

failures.condition: The option id is unknown or belongs to a different poll.
failures.recovery: Choose one of the options displayed for the active poll.
failures.response: The write is rejected as option_not_in_poll and the tally is unchanged.

failures.condition: The voter code is empty or whitespace only.
failures.recovery: Enter a nonblank personal code and submit again.
failures.response: The write is rejected as code_required and nothing is stored.

failures.condition: The store cannot be written or the write is interrupted.
failures.recovery: Retry the submission; if the failure persists, inspect the store file before accepting further ballots.
failures.response: The write is rejected as store_unwritable and neither the ballot nor the aggregate changes.

actions.name: Submit or replace a ballot
preconditions: The poll status is open.
The submitted code is nonblank after trimming.
The submitted option id belongs to this poll.
The local store is writable.

effects: Poll status becomes closed and closed_at is set.
A closed event is appended with its timestamp.
The tally becomes final and its current counts are preserved.

failures.condition: The poll is already closed.
failures.recovery: Reopen the poll first if voting must continue.
failures.response: The close is rejected as already_closed and no duplicate event is written.

failures.condition: The host session is locked.
failures.recovery: Unlock host mode with the passphrase, then close again.
failures.response: The close is rejected as host_mode_required and the poll stays open.

actions.name: Close the poll
preconditions: The host session is unlocked on this device.
The poll status is open.

effects: Poll status becomes open again, closed_at is cleared, and reopen_count increments.
A reopened event is appended with its timestamp.
All existing ballots remain untouched and the tally returns to provisional with the same counts.

failures.condition: The poll is already open.
failures.recovery: Proceed with voting; no reopen is needed.
failures.response: The reopen is rejected as already_open and nothing changes.

failures.condition: The host session is locked.
failures.recovery: Unlock host mode with the passphrase, then reopen.
failures.response: The reopen is rejected as host_mode_required and the poll stays closed.

actions.name: Reopen the poll
preconditions: The host session is unlocked on this device.
The poll status is closed.

effects: Per-option counts are recomputed from stored ballots, including zero-count options.
total_ballots is reported alongside the counts and the tie set is computed from the highest count.
No code-to-choice mapping is exposed to members.

failures.condition: The poll id does not exist in the local store.
failures.recovery: Return to the poll index or the setup surface and choose an existing poll.
failures.response: The read returns poll_not_found and no counts are shown.

failures.condition: The store cannot be read or parsed.
failures.recovery: Inspect the local store file, restore from the last intact state, or recreate the poll; the application must not overwrite the unreadable file silently.
failures.response: The read returns store_unreadable and the surface shows an error state without inventing counts.

actions.name: Read the aggregate
preconditions: The poll exists in the directory store and its store is readable.
The caller is on this device and the poll is the active poll.

effects: The chosen poll id becomes the active poll for every subsequent read and write.
Only that poll's options, ballots, events, and aggregate are loaded, and the previous poll's data is no longer addressable from the voting or result surfaces.

failures.condition: The requested poll id is not present in the store.
failures.recovery: Choose one of the poll rows listed by the index.
failures.response: The selection returns poll_not_found and the previously active poll stays active.

failures.condition: The store cannot be read or parsed.
failures.recovery: Restore an intact store copy before selecting a poll.
failures.response: The selection returns store_unreadable and no poll becomes active.

actions.name: Select the active poll
preconditions: At least one poll exists in the directory store.
The store is readable.

effects: Returns in_use when the trimmed code already holds a ballot on the active poll and unused otherwise.
Returns no option id, label, timestamp, or revision for an in-use code, so the check cannot disclose another member's choice.

failures.condition: The submitted code is blank or whitespace only.
failures.recovery: Enter the code to check and submit again.
failures.response: The check is rejected as code_required and no status is reported.

failures.condition: The active poll no longer exists in the store.
failures.recovery: Return to the poll index and select an existing poll.
failures.response: The check returns poll_not_found and no status is reported.

actions.name: Check whether a code already holds a ballot
preconditions: The active poll exists and the store is readable.

assertions.given: A poll exists on the shared device and the host session is locked, so the device is in member mode.
assertions.negative: A locked session must never authorize a host transition, and no host control may become usable merely because the member voting page was reloaded.
assertions.then: All three member attempts are refused as host_mode_required with no poll or status change, while the host's unlocked close succeeds and sets status closed with a closed event.
assertions.when: A member tries to create another poll, close the open poll, and reopen it, and then the host unlocks with the passphrase and repeats the close.

assertions.given: The host session is unlocked after a poll was created and two ballots exist.
assertions.negative: An unlocked session must not survive the handoff or a process restart, and locking must not alter poll status, ballots, events, or counts.
assertions.then: Host controls disappear, the close attempt is refused as host_mode_required, and after restart the session is locked again with the poll and both ballots intact.
assertions.when: The host locks host mode, a member tries to close the poll, and the process is stopped and started again in the same directory.

assertions.given: An unlocked host session on a directory store and a nonblank dinner question.
assertions.negative: Creation must not store a poll without a created event, and it must not store options as free text without poll-scoped ids.
assertions.then: The poll is stored open with created_at, one option row per label in entry order with poll-scoped ids, a created event at the creation timestamp, and a provisional tally with every option at 0 and total 0.
assertions.when: The host creates a poll with three distinct place labels.

assertions.given: The host is on the setup surface with an unlocked host session and a nonblank question.
assertions.negative: Accepting 1 option leaves nothing to choose between and accepting 9 exceeds the stated instrument size; neither may be stored.
assertions.then: The 1-option and 9-option submissions are rejected as option_count_invalid, while the 3-label submission creates an open poll with three option rows.
assertions.when: The host submits 1 option, then 9 options, then a set of 3 distinct labels.

assertions.given: The host is on the setup surface with an unlocked host session and a nonblank question.
assertions.negative: A stored set with an empty or indistinguishable label would make later ballots and counts ambiguous.
assertions.then: Creation is rejected as option_label_invalid, the offending label is identified, and no poll or option row is stored.
assertions.when: The host submits labels that include a blank entry or two labels equal after trimming and case folding, such as Pizza and pizza.

assertions.given: A poll in open status has options A and B and no ballots.
assertions.negative: If the second submission reused ana as the code it must replace ana's ballot with B, leaving A=0 and total=1; a second row for ana or a total of 2 under one code would both be wrong.
assertions.then: The tally reports A=1, B=1, total=2, and each code appears in exactly one stored ballot.
assertions.when: Member ana submits a ballot for A and member bo submits a ballot for B on the same device.

assertions.given: The poll has ballots ana to A and bo to B with total 2.
assertions.negative: If a replacement appended a second row the total would read 3 or A would still show 1; both are wrong.
assertions.then: Exactly one ana ballot remains, now on B, and the tally reads A=0, B=2, total=2.
assertions.when: Member ana re-submits with the same code ana, choosing B.

assertions.given: Poll P1 has options A and B and poll P2 has options C and D, with P1 active.
assertions.negative: Accepting the foreign option would create a phantom row in P1 or leak P2's totals into P1.
assertions.then: The P1 submission is rejected as option_not_in_poll, P1's tally is unchanged, and P2's ballot counts only in P2.
assertions.when: A ballot for P1 is submitted using P2's option C, and separately a ballot for P2 uses D after selecting P2.

assertions.given: The poll is open and no ballot exists for the entered code.
assertions.negative: Accepting blank codes would collapse different members into one anonymous ballot and undercount the group.
assertions.then: The write is rejected as code_required, no ballot is stored, and the tally is unchanged.
assertions.when: A member submits a choice with an empty or whitespace-only code.

assertions.given: Any stored ballot set exists for a poll with zero-count options.
assertions.negative: A total larger than the number of distinct codes, or a tally that omits zero-count options or borrows another poll's options, is invalid.
assertions.then: The sum of per-option counts equals the number of distinct stored codes, every row corresponds to an option of this poll, and zero-count options are shown as 0.
assertions.when: The aggregate is read.

assertions.given: A poll holds an equal split such as A=2 and B=2, or any shared highest count.
assertions.negative: Naming the first or last option as winner, or hiding one tied option, misreports the group's answer.
assertions.then: Both options show the equal count and the view states that the result is a tie, listing every tied option and naming no winner.
assertions.when: The tally is displayed.

assertions.given: A poll has options and several ballots and the tally has been read once.
assertions.negative: If the store were re-initialized, partially written, or a ballot replayed on start, counts would change or double.
assertions.then: The poll reloads with the same status, the same option set, the same per-option counts and total, and no duplicated or replayed ballot.
assertions.when: The page is refreshed and the process is stopped and started again in the same application directory.

assertions.given: A poll directory whose store file has been truncated or corrupted after a previous successful read.
assertions.negative: The aggregate must never fall back to zero counts, a partially parsed ballot set, or a fabricated winner, and the store must not be overwritten silently.
assertions.then: The read returns store_unreadable, the surface shows an explicit error with no counts, no total, and no winner, and the corrupted file is left in place for inspection.
assertions.when: Either role opens the voting or result surface and the aggregate is requested.

assertions.given: An open poll has one ballot for code ana on option A and the tally has just been displayed.
assertions.negative: If ballots lived only in memory, or if startup replayed a stored write, the count would drop to zero or double instead of staying at one.
assertions.then: The ballot is re-read with the same code and option, the per-option counts and total are identical, and no ballot is duplicated or replayed.
assertions.when: The surface is refreshed and the process is stopped and started again in the same application directory.

assertions.given: A poll with total 2 is in open status and the host session is unlocked.
assertions.negative: A closed poll that stored the write, dropped a prior ballot, or altered the aggregate would break the freeze.
assertions.then: The write is rejected with response poll_closed and the tally remains total 2 with identical per-option counts.
assertions.when: The host closes it and a member then submits a new ballot under a new code.

assertions.given: A closed poll holds a ballot for code ana on option A.
assertions.negative: Letting an existing voter move a vote after close would change a result the host declared final.
assertions.then: The replacement is rejected with poll_closed, ana's ballot keeps A, and the aggregate is unchanged.
assertions.when: Ana re-submits with the same code choosing B.

assertions.given: A closed poll holds ballots A=1 and B=1, total 2, and the host session is unlocked.
assertions.negative: If reopening cleared ballots or added a second ballot for an existing code the total would not be 3 with those per-option counts.
assertions.then: Status is open, a reopened event is appended, both prior ballots are intact, and the tally reads A=2, B=1, total=3.
assertions.when: The host reopens the poll and member cy votes for A.

assertions.given: A poll holds two ballots and the host has moved it to closed status, while the shared device still shows the member voting surface.
assertions.negative: Neither a first ballot under a new code nor a replacement under an existing code may be stored while the poll is closed, and the aggregate must not shift by even one count.
assertions.then: Both writes are rejected with response poll_closed, no ballot row is added or changed, and the tally still reports the two original ballots with unchanged per-option counts.
assertions.when: A member submits a first ballot under a new code, and a different member re-submits with an existing code to change their choice.

assertions.given: An open poll with two ballots and an unlocked host session.
assertions.negative: A close must not be recorded only in status without an event, and a repeated close must not append a duplicate event or alter counts.
assertions.then: Status becomes closed with closed_at, exactly one closed event is appended, the tally becomes final with unchanged counts, and the repeat close is rejected as already_closed without a second event.
assertions.when: The host closes the poll and then submits a second close.

assertions.given: Member ana has voted and opens the voting surface again.
assertions.negative: Showing other codes next to their choices would expose individual ballots that the aggregate does not require.
assertions.then: Per-option counts and the total are visible, while no other member's code is paired with a choice anywhere on the surface.
assertions.when: The tally is rendered for ana.

assertions.given: One directory holds polls P1 with options A and B and P2 with options C and D, each with one ballot, and P1 is active.
assertions.negative: Selecting another poll must not carry over ballots, options, or counts, and an option id from the inactive poll must never enter the active poll's tally.
assertions.then: P2's tally shows only C and D with its own total, P1's tally shows only A and B, and the P1 submission using P2's option is rejected as option_not_in_poll.
assertions.when: A member selects P2, submits a ballot for option C, then selects P1 and submits option C to P1.

assertions.given: An open poll where code ana holds a ballot for option A.
assertions.negative: The check must never return the option, label, or ballot age for an in-use code, because that would expose another member's choice on a shared screen.
assertions.then: The first check reports in_use without revealing A or any timestamp, the second reports unused, and the blank check is rejected as code_required.
assertions.when: A member checks ana, then checks a code that has not voted, then checks a blank code.

basis.statement: The host creates one dinner question with a fixed set of 2-8 place options before voting starts.
Members vote on the same device under a self-chosen code, one option per person, and re-submitting with the same code replaces the earlier choice so the person still holds exactly one vote.
A per-option tally is the visible deliverable, with a total that stays at 2 when two members choose different options and 2 again after one replaces their choice.
The host can close the poll, after which further votes return poll_closed and the stored result is unchanged, and can reopen it so a third member can vote for a total of 3.
A vote option must belong to the poll being voted on, duplicate and empty option labels and empty codes must be rejected, and votes from different polls must never merge.
Poll state and aggregate survive a page refresh and a process restart in the same directory, and a tie is displayed as a tie rather than resolved by an arbitrary winner.
The upstream product is a Nextcloud server application written in PHP and JS/Vue and described as a free meeting-schedule tool similar to Doodle, not a standalone same-device poll page.
The poll entity declares table polls_polls with the types datePoll and textPoll plus a simple voting variant, oriented to date or text option scheduling rather than a generic single-choice question.
A vote answer is stored per option as yes, no, or maybe, and the poll entity carries an allowMaybe setting alongside its result-visibility setting.

Vote rows are soft-deleted records carrying poll id, user id, option id, an option text snapshot, an option hash, and an answer, so a vote is bound to a poll and an option record rather than to free text.
Option identity in the vote is cryptographically derived from the poll id plus the option text, and a separate accessor exposes the stored hash so text and hash mismatches can be detected.

Poll lifecycle is driven by an integer expiry timestamp: a poll is expired when expire is greater than zero and less than now, and voting is denied while expired; no explicit open or closed boolean or reopen field appears.
Archival is separate from closing: a deleted timestamp marks the poll archived, and the status payload distinguishes archived from expired.
Result visibility is a three-way setting of always, closed, or never; editors always see results, participants see them per the setting, and the legacy value expired is mapped to closed.
Participation identity is a Nextcloud user identity: polls store an owner id, votes store a user id, and voting is restricted to external, user, or admin user types.
Anonymity is a poll setting with a lockable state: a negative anonymous value means real anonymous and cannot be changed back.
Access is private or open, and the poll declares the roles owner, admin, user, email, contact, external, and none for sharing and participation.
Changing another participant's votes and deanonymizing are gated separately on an anonymity value above -1, edit rights, and an unrestricted poll owner.
Participant option creation is a proposal mode of disallow, allow, or review with an optional proposal expiry, and public shares are barred from adding options.
Vote volume controls exist as maxVotesPerUser and maxVotesPerOption, limits on votes rather than on the number of poll options.
createClone builds a fresh entity titled Clone of ... with a new owner, private access, anonymity reset to 0, expiry and settings copied, and no votes.

The pinned README bullets advertise hiding results until the owner reveals them, obfuscating participant names or strong anonymous mode, automatic expiry, participant-added options, vote limits per option or user, spreadsheet or HTML export, confirming options after closing, and a REST API, with screenshots for managing and creating polls, configuration, sharing, and mobile voting.

The README states the app is not maintained by Nextcloud despite living in the Nextcloud GitHub organisation, and its screenshots describe managing and creating polls, many configuration options, sharing a poll, and voting on mobile.

COPYING carries the GNU Affero General Public License version 3 text and lib/Db/Vote.php declares SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later; the snapshot records license_status fixed_notice_located_spdx_not_independently_verified.
Upstream was not executed: the snapshot records upstream_status not_run, so all upstream statements are static readings of four pinned files rather than observed behavior.
The supplied upstream inventory is only COPYING, README.md, lib/Db/Poll.php, and lib/Db/Vote.php; routing, controllers, services, mappers, migrations, and frontend are absent.

Model closing and reopening as explicit host-owned poll status transitions with recorded events, instead of reusing an expiry timestamp as the only way to stop voting, so a closed poll rejects writes with poll_closed and a reopened poll accepts new voters.

Represent a ballot as poll id plus pseudonym code plus one option id with uniqueness on poll id and code, so re-submitting a code replaces that ballot in place and the aggregate is recomputed from ballots.
Give options stable poll-scoped ids, validate that a ballot's option belongs to the same poll, and reject duplicate or empty option labels at creation.
Use one durable local store in the application directory with atomic writes and derive totals from stored ballots on load, so refresh and same-directory restart reproduce identical state.
Display ties as equal counts with every tied option listed, no winner designation, and no synthesized tiebreaker.
Separate a host setup and control surface from a member voting and result surface, both usable sequentially on one device without per-member accounts.

Borrow upstream configurability only where it maps to this scenario and leave out accounts, shares, groups, REST API, reminders, comments, calendar integration, anonymity machinery, option proposals, and hidden-results settings.

Replace upstream's Nextcloud user identity with a device-local host passphrase and an explicit host-mode session: host transitions require an unlocked session, members need no identity beyond their ballot code, and the session relocks on explicit lock or process restart.
Expose an explicit poll index that sets one active poll id per directory, so several polls can coexist while every option, ballot, event, and count stays scoped to its poll.

Expose a read-only code-status check that reports only whether a code already holds a ballot on the active poll, never the chosen option, so a member can avoid an accidental replacement without breaking aggregate-only privacy.

How the upstream aggregate is computed and displayed, including counts, percentages, charts, total participants, and tie presentation, cannot be determined because no tally, mapper, controller, or frontend file is in the supplied inventory.
Upstream reopen-after-close behavior is unknown; the supplied entity exposes only expire and deleted, and no reopen action was read.
Whether upstream supports same-device sequential voting under self-declared pseudonyms without accounts is unknown and is contradicted by the user-type gate on voting.
Upstream rejection of duplicate option labels, empty option labels, or empty participant identifiers is not evidenced in the supplied files.
No upstream rule limiting a poll to 2-8 options was found; the discovered limits apply to votes per user and votes per option.
Runtime behavior, persistence across restarts, and any error code such as poll_closed were neither executed nor observed upstream because upstream_status is not_run.

journeys.completion: The poll exists in open status with a recorded created event and every option has a stable id usable by ballots.
journeys.goal: Establish host control on the shared device and produce an open poll with a question and a valid fixed option set ready for the first voter.
journeys.name: Host unlocks and sets up the dinner poll
journeys.recovery: On a validation failure the host corrects the option count or labels and resubmits; creation is atomic, so no partial poll or option set remains. A rejected passphrase leaves member voting available and the host retries the passphrase.

steps.success: Host mode unlocks with the passphrase and the question and option fields become available.
The poll is stored as open with 2-8 distinct options, a created event, and a provisional all-zero tally.

journeys.completion: The device is in member mode, host transitions require the passphrase again, and ballots record and tally without a host session.
journeys.goal: Return the shared device to the group with host controls unavailable and voting fully usable.
journeys.name: Host locks the console and hands the device over
journeys.recovery: If a host control is still visible the host locks again; a member who reaches a host-only entry receives host_mode_required and continues on the voting surface.

steps.success: Host controls disappear and the console returns to the passphrase prompt.
A ballot is recorded under the member's code with no host session available on the device.
The aggregate is readable without host mode and shows the recorded counts.

journeys.completion: Two distinct codes hold two ballots, the changed ballot replaced rather than added, and the total remains 2.
journeys.goal: Collect one ballot per member on a shared device and keep the total stable when a member replaces their choice.
journeys.name: Two members vote and one changes their mind
journeys.recovery: If a member forgets their code they would create a new ballot under a new code, so the code-status check and the retained code field make an accidental second ballot visible; re-submission with the same code always replaces.

steps.success: Member ana's ballot for option A is stored and the tally shows total 1.
Member bo's ballot for option B is stored and the tally shows A=1, B=1, total 2.
The aggregate is visible as A=1, B=1, total 2.
Ana re-submits with code ana for B, the ballot is replaced in place, and the tally becomes A=0, B=2, total 2.

journeys.completion: The close genuinely freezes writes, the reopen restores voting without clearing history, and the final total is 3.
journeys.goal: Stop all writes at close, prove the aggregate is frozen, then admit a further voter after an explicit reopen.
journeys.name: Host freezes the result and later reopens
journeys.recovery: A member whose write hit poll_closed waits for the host to reopen and submits again with the same code, so no duplicate ballot is created; an attempted close or reopen without an unlocked session returns host_mode_required.

steps.success: Host mode unlocks and the close control becomes available.
Status becomes closed, a closed event is recorded, and the tally is final at total 2.
Host mode locks so the device can be handed back while the poll stays closed.
The attempt is rejected with poll_closed and the tally still shows total 2 with unchanged per-option counts.
The host unlocks again and the reopen control appears.
Status returns to open, a reopened event is recorded, and both existing ballots remain.
Host mode locks again and the device is returned to the group in open status.
A third member cy votes for A and the tally becomes total 3.
The result view shows the three-ballot aggregate with the prior ballots preserved.

journeys.completion: State, options, ballots, and counts are identical across refresh and restart, and a tie is displayed as a tie.
journeys.goal: Confirm the aggregate is derived from durable ballots and that an equal split is reported as a tie without a winner.
journeys.name: Aggregate survives refresh and restart, tie shown honestly
journeys.recovery: If the store read fails the view states store_unreadable and does not fall back to zero counts or a fabricated winner; the host restores an intact store copy.

steps.success: Before reload the tally reports the recorded counts and total for the poll.
After a page refresh and a same-directory process restart the same counts and total reappear with no duplicate ballots and host mode locked again.
When two options share the highest count the view lists both and states that the result is a tie, naming no winner.

journeys.completion: Two polls coexist with separate options, ballots, events, and counts, and switching the active poll cannot merge them.
journeys.goal: Operate more than one poll in the same directory while keeping each poll's options, ballots, and counts separate.
journeys.name: Two polls coexist without mixing
journeys.recovery: If an option id from the inactive poll is submitted after switching, it is rejected as option_not_in_poll and the member reselects the option shown for the active poll.

steps.success: Poll P1 becomes active and only P1's options and tally are listed.
A ballot for P1 is stored and P2 remains untouched.
Poll P2 becomes active with its own options and its own ballots.
P2's aggregate shows only P2's ballots and total.

product_shape.audience: A small group standing around one shared device deciding where to eat, plus one host who sets up, unlocks, and controls the poll; no member accounts, invitations, or remote participants.
product_shape.boundary: One directory store holds one or more polls, and the poll index sets which poll is active. Each poll is one question with a fixed set of 2-8 predefined place options, identified by a poll id that scopes its options, ballots, aggregate, and lifecycle events. Members identify themselves only by a self-chosen code at the moment of voting, hold exactly one ballot per poll, and replace that ballot by re-submitting the same code. Host-only transitions (create, close, reopen) require an unlocked host session established with the device-local passphrase; members never need that session. The tally is always computed from stored ballots, survives refresh and a same-directory process restart, and reports ties as ties.
product_shape.delivery_profile: Single-device browser application served from one application directory with a local durable store and a device-local host passphrase; host mode and member voting are used sequentially on the same screen, with no server accounts, network distribution, or background services.
excluded: Per-member accounts, login, passwords, email verification, or any remote identity provider; host mode is a local passphrase gate, not an account system
Share links, QR codes, embeds, chat or meeting-platform distribution, and multi-device concurrent access
Multiple questions per poll, survey batteries, and per-response processing workflows
Multiple-choice, rating, ranking, dot-voting, yes/no/maybe per option, and weighted vote semantics
Participant-added options, option editing or deletion after voting starts, and option proposal review
Comments, discussion threads, reminders, notifications, calendar conflict hints, and exports
Anonymity modes, obfuscated participant names, deanonymization, and who-voted-what listings
Hidden or delayed result visibility, per-user or per-option vote caps, automatic expiry dates, archival, cloning, and deletion workflows
REST API, admin dashboards across a workspace, and Nextcloud group or contact integration
Bot detection, CAPTCHA, address- or cookie-based duplicate voting, and vote tokens
product_shape.name: Same-Device Dinner Poll
product_shape.value: The group gets one trustworthy per-option tally of a single dinner question, with one ballot per self-chosen code, a frozen result while closed, a preserved aggregate across refresh and process restart, and host control gated by a device-local passphrase rather than accounts.

roles.data_scope: All poll configuration, the option set, aggregate counts and totals, poll status, the close/reopen event log, and the device-local host passphrase verifier and session state; no listing that maps other members' codes to their choices.
roles.goal: Pose one dinner question with a fixed option set, keep the poll open while the group votes, close it to freeze the result, and reopen it only when the group needs to continue, unlocking host mode on the shared device when control is needed.
roles.name: Host

roles.data_scope: The question, the option set, the aggregate counts and total, whether their own code already holds a ballot, and the state of their own ballot after entering the code; other members' code-to-choice mappings are not exposed.
roles.goal: Express one place preference under a personal code, replace that preference without gaining a second vote, and read the current aggregate.
roles.name: Member

rules.statement: A poll carries exactly one question and between 2 and 8 predefined options; a creation with fewer than 2 or more than 8 options fails and stores nothing.
Each option has a stable id scoped to its poll; labels are trimmed and case-folded for duplicate detection, and blank or duplicate labels are rejected before anything is stored.
A ballot is uniquely identified by poll id plus voter code; the code must be nonblank, and submitting again with the same code replaces that ballot instead of adding a second one.
A ballot's option must belong to the same poll as the ballot; an unknown option or an option from another poll is rejected and never recorded.
All reads and writes are scoped by the active poll id, so options, ballots, events, and counts from different polls never mix and a foreign option cannot enter another poll's aggregate.
While a poll is closed, every ballot write, new or replaced, is rejected with response poll_closed and the stored ballots and aggregate remain unchanged.
Reopening sets the poll back to open, appends a reopened event, keeps every existing ballot, and admits new codes and replacements under the same open-poll rules.

The aggregate is recomputed from stored ballots on every read: one count per option including zeros, a total equal to the number of distinct codes, and all options sharing the highest count reported as tied with no winner field.

Poll state, options, ballots, and lifecycle events live in one local store inside the application directory, written atomically and reloaded at start, so refresh and same-directory process restart reproduce the same status and aggregate.

Only a caller holding the unlocked host session may create, close, or reopen a poll; members may submit or replace their own ballot and read the aggregate, and no member surface exposes host controls.
A member's code is used only to locate their own ballot; the aggregate and the code-status check expose no code-to-choice mapping, so no member can read another member's individual choice.

Host-only actions require an unlocked host session; a fresh directory has no passphrase and the first unlock sets one, unlocking needs that passphrase, and the session relocks on explicit lock or process restart and is never inferred from the member voting surface.

scope_options.name: Same-device dinner poll with host mode, close and reopen
scope_options.rationale: The scenario's own loop and every acceptance rule: a passphrase-gated host creates the poll, members ballot and replace under one code, the host closes and reopens, the tally is derived from durable ballots, and ties are shown as ties. Including close and reopen keeps the closed-write rule reachable inside the slice, and durability is inherent because ballot and tally actions read and write the same store.

scope_options.name: Several polls coexisting in one directory
scope_options.rationale: The acceptance rule that different polls never mix implies more than one poll can exist; this slice adds the poll index and its selection action so the active poll id is explicit while every option, ballot, event, and count stays scoped to its poll.

scope_options.name: Voter code status check before submitting
scope_options.rationale: Because a code is the ballot key, a member reusing a taken code silently replaces that ballot; this slice adds a read-only check that reports only whether a code is in use, never the chosen option, so a collision is visible without weakening aggregate-only privacy.
